easy.def: A large insect that makes a loud buzzing sound.
examples: A cicada buzzed.
Cicadas are loud.
I heard a cicada.

more.def: A large bug with clear wings that makes a loud, buzzing sound.
examples: The cicada buzzed in the tree.
Cicadas spend years underground before they come out.
The summer air hummed with the song of cicadas.

easy.def: A drink made from apples.
examples: We drank apple cider.
The cider is sweet.
Warm cider is tasty.

more.def: A drink made by squeezing apples, often served warm in the fall.
examples: We drank warm apple cider on the hayride.
The farmer pressed apples to make fresh cider.
Cider tastes sweet and a little tart.

easy.def: A green plant used to flavor food.
examples: I smell cilantro.
The cilantro is green.
Dad added cilantro to the dish.

more.def: A green plant with soft leaves used to flavor food.
examples: Mom chopped fresh cilantro for the tacos.
Cilantro has a bright, fresh smell.
We grew cilantro in a pot on the porch.

easy.def: Something that is very easy.
examples: The test was a cinch.
Tying shoes is a cinch.
It is a cinch.

more.def: Something that is very easy to do.
examples: The test was a cinch because I had studied.
Making a sandwich is a cinch.
Riding a bike is a cinch once you know how.

easy.def: A small piece of wood that has burned.
examples: A cinder fell from the fire.
The cinders were hot.
Cinders were gray.

more.def: A small piece of wood or coal that has been burned but is still hot or glowing.
examples: A glowing cinder popped out of the fire.
Cinders covered the floor of the fireplace.
The cinders cooled slowly after the fire went out.

easy.def: A place where you go to watch movies.
examples: We went to the cinema.
The cinema is big.
I saw a movie at the cinema.

more.def: A building where movies are shown, or the art of making movies.
examples: We went to the cinema to watch the new cartoon.
The cinema had a big screen and soft seats.
She studies cinema and wants to make her own movies.

easy.def: A sweet brown spice that smells good.
examples: I like cinnamon on toast.
The cookies had cinnamon.
The cinnamon smells sweet.

more.def: A sweet-smelling brown spice made from the bark of a tree, often used in baking.
examples: Mom sprinkled cinnamon on the apple slices before she baked them.
Cinnamon comes from the bark of a tropical tree.
The whole kitchen smelled of warm cinnamon rolls.

easy.def: A secret code.
examples: They wrote in cipher.
The cipher was hard.
He solved the cipher.

more.def: A secret way of writing, in which letters or numbers stand for other letters.
examples: The spies wrote their message in a cipher.
She solved the cipher by switching the letters.
The children made up a cipher to pass secret notes.

easy.def: A round shape.
examples: Draw a circle.
The sun is a circle.
The kids sat in a circle.

more.def: A perfectly round shape, like a ring.
examples: Draw a circle with the compass.
The children sat in a circle on the rug.
A circle has no corners.

easy.def: To go around.
examples: The birds circle.
The plane circled.
She circled the answer.

more.def: To move around something in a ring, or to draw a ring around something.
examples: Hawks circled high above the field.
Circle the right answer on your paper.
The plane circled before landing.

easy.def: A path that electricity flows along.
examples: The circuit has a battery.
A circuit makes the light work.
The circuit is broken.

more.def: A complete path along which electricity can flow.
examples: The circuit has a battery and a bulb.
A broken circuit made the light go out.
We built a simple circuit in science class.

easy.def: Round like a circle.
examples: The table is circular.
A circular path.
The mirror is circular.

more.def: Shaped like a circle, or moving around in a circle.
examples: The table was circular, so everyone could see each other.
We walked along a circular path around the pond.
The circular saw spun very fast.

easy.def: To move around and around.
examples: Blood circulates in your body.
Air circulates in the room.
The fan circulates the air.

more.def: To move around in a circle, or to pass from one place or person to another.
examples: Blood circulates through your body, carried by your heart.
A fan helped circulate the air in the stuffy room.
The teacher circulated around the classroom to help each group.

easy.def: The flow of blood around your body.
examples: Exercise helps circulation.
Good circulation keeps your hands warm.
Poor circulation makes my feet cold.

more.def: The movement of blood around the body, or of air or water through a place.
examples: Exercise helps your circulation.
Good circulation keeps your hands and feet warm.
Open windows give the room good air circulation.

easy.def: The number of copies of a paper or magazine that are sold.
examples: The paper has a big circulation.
The magazine's circulation grew.
A large circulation.

more.def: The number of copies of a newspaper or magazine that are sold or given out.
examples: The paper has a circulation of ten thousand.
The school magazine has a small circulation.
The magazine's circulation grew each month.

easy.def: About the flow of blood in the body.
examples: The circulatory system.
A circulatory problem.
The circulatory path.

more.def: Having to do with the movement of blood around the body.
examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system.
The circulatory system carries blood through the body.
Exercise helps your circulatory health.

easy.def: The distance around a circle.
examples: Measure the circumference.
The circumference is long.
The circle's circumference.

more.def: The distance all the way around the edge of a circle.
examples: We measured the circumference of the tree trunk.
The circumference of the circle is about twelve inches.
The Earth's circumference is about twenty-five thousand miles.

easy.def: A fact or condition that affects what happens.
examples: In that circumstance, we stayed home.
The circumstances were hard.
Rain was a circumstance we did not expect.

more.def: A fact or condition connected to an event, which can change what you do.
examples: Under the circumstances, we decided to cancel the picnic.
The circumstances of the storm made it hard to travel.
Her circumstances changed when she moved to a new town.

easy.def: A show with clowns, animals and people who do tricks.
examples: We saw a circus.
The clown is at the circus.
The circus came to town.

more.def: A traveling show with clowns, acrobats and animals that perform tricks.
examples: We saw lions and clowns at the circus.
The circus put up a big tent in town.
An acrobat swung above the crowd at the circus.

easy.def: A big tank for storing water.
examples: The cistern holds water.
The cistern is full.
A cistern is under the house.

more.def: A large tank that is used to store water, especially rainwater.
examples: The house had a cistern to collect rainwater.
The old cistern held enough water for the whole summer.
A cistern stood beside the barn.

easy.def: A strong castle on a hill.
examples: The citadel is on the hill.
The citadel was strong.
We saw the citadel.

more.def: A strong fort built on high ground to protect a city.
examples: The citadel stood on the hill above the city.
Soldiers once guarded the citadel.
From the top of the citadel, you can see for miles.

easy.def: To mention as proof or example.
examples: She cited a book.
He cited the rule.
They cite examples.

more.def: To name something as proof or as an example.
examples: She cited a book to prove her point.
He cited the rule about homework.
Scientists cite many studies.

easy.def: A person who belongs to a country or town.
examples: My dad is a citizen of this country.
The citizens of the town voted.
A good citizen helps others.

more.def: A person who lives in a place and has rights there, such as a town or country.
examples: Every citizen can vote when they are eighteen.
The mayor thanked the citizens for cleaning the park.
She became a citizen of the United States last year.

easy.def: Being a member of a country, and doing your part.
examples: She got her citizenship.
Good citizenship means helping.
He learned about citizenship.

more.def: The state of being a member of a country, or the way a person acts as a member of a community.
examples: She became a member of the country by earning citizenship.
The class talked about good citizenship and helping neighbors.
Picking up litter shows good citizenship.

easy.def: Fruits like oranges and lemons.
examples: Oranges are citrus.
A lemon is citrus.
I like citrus.

more.def: A group of fruits such as oranges, lemons and limes that have a sour or sweet juice.
examples: Oranges and lemons are citrus fruits.
The citrus trees grew in the warm yard.
I like the fresh smell of citrus.

easy.def: A big town with many people.
examples: Many people live in a city.
The city has tall buildings.
We drove to the city.

more.def: A large town where many people live and work.
examples: The city has tall buildings, busy streets and a huge library.
Millions of people ride the subway in this city every day.
Cities are often built beside rivers or harbors.

easy.def: In the whole city.
examples: A citywide cleanup.
The citywide sale.
A citywide contest.

more.def: Happening in or including a whole city.
examples: A citywide cleanup day was held.
The citywide contest had many winners.
A citywide bus service began.

easy.def: About a town and its people.
examples: It is a civic duty.
The civic center.
A civic event.

more.def: Having to do with a town or city and its citizens.
examples: Voting is a civic duty.
The civic center holds concerts.
Neighbors held a civic meeting.

easy.def: Polite.
examples: Be civil to the guests.
He gave a civil answer.
She is civil.

more.def: Polite and respectful, even when you do not agree.
examples: Be civil to your guests.
He gave a civil reply, even though he was upset.
Please keep the talk civil.

easy.def: Having to do with the people of a country.
examples: People have civil rights.
Voting is a civil duty.
The civil government makes laws.

more.def: Having to do with the ordinary people and affairs of a country.
examples: Jury service is a civil duty.
People fought for their civil rights.
The civil government runs the town.

easy.def: A person who is not in the army.
examples: A civilian lives in town.
He is a civilian.
The civilians were safe.

more.def: A person who is not in the military or the police.
examples: She is a civilian, not a soldier.
Civilians were told to stay home.
The pilot had been a soldier, but now he is a civilian.

easy.def: A group of people with a way of life that includes cities and writing.
examples: The Egyptians had a great civilization.
The civilization built pyramids.
We learned about an ancient civilization.

more.def: A society that has cities, laws, writing and art, such as ancient Egypt.
examples: The ancient Egyptians built a great civilization along the Nile.
Historians study the civilization of ancient Greece.
The Mayan civilization built stone temples.

easy.def: To teach better manners.
examples: The teacher tried to civilize them.
Civilize the class.
Manners civilize us.

more.def: To bring a group of people to a more developed way of life; or to teach good manners.
examples: The teacher tried to civilize the rowdy class.
Good manners help civilize us.
The story tells how the princess tried to civilize the wild boy.

easy.def: Polite and well behaved.
examples: The civilized guests were polite.
He is civilized.
A civilized talk.

more.def: Having good manners and a well-ordered way of living.
examples: The guests were calm and civilized.
They had a civilized talk and settled their differences.
A civilized person waits for a turn.
